manifest.title: Redis
manifest.author: Redis Ltd.
manifest.tagline: In-memory data store, reachable over TLS
manifest.description:
Redis is an in-memory data store used as a cache, message broker and database. This package installs Redis from the official Redis APT repository (packages.redis.io). It exposes Redis on a TCP port that only accepts TLS connections with a password.

### This package

* TLS with the app domain's certificate from Cloudron. Clients connect with `rediss://default:<password>@<app domain>:<port>`.
* A random password is generated on first start (`/app/data/credentials.env`).
* Data is persisted with AOF and RDB snapshots in `/app/data/redis` and included in Cloudron backups.
* `maxmemory` is set to 75% of the app's memory limit. Change the memory limit in the app's resource settings.
* Your own settings go into `/app/data/redis.conf`.
manifest.postInstallMessage:
Redis only accepts TLS connections with a password. The password was generated on first start and is in `/app/data/credentials.env`. Open it with the File Manager or the Web Terminal.

Connection URL:

```
rediss://default:<password>@$CLOUDRON-APP-DOMAIN:<port>
```

`<port>` is the TCP port you chose during installation (default `6380`). Cloudron opens it in the firewall. It is reachable from the internet, so keep the password secret.

For Sockudo from the same repository, put this into Sockudo's `/app/data/env.sh`:

```
export SOCKUDO_REDIS_URL="rediss://default:<password>@$CLOUDRON-APP-DOMAIN:<port>/0"
```
